title: Aureline benchmark reference-hardware-profile object
description: Boundary schema for a single benchmark reference-hardware-profile object. A reference-hardware profile is the canonical identity of one machine class a benchmark claim may cite: its stable id, whether it is a council-approved reference_lab row or a self_capture placeholder, its display class, default power posture, the lab-image revision it pairs with, its council status, the workload classes it is approved to back, and the canonical hardware register it projects from. A claim-bearing metric must bind a reference_lab profile that is council-approved; a self_capture row must declare not_reference_eligible_without_promotion so local developer hardware cannot masquerade as a protected reference row. A profile with no display class or no lab-image identity fails closed. Raw machine labels, serial numbers, and host names never cross this boundary; only stable ids and reviewable sentences do.

hardware_profile_ref.description: Stable hardware-definition id resolvable in the canonical reference-hardware register; never a raw machine label.

lab_image_ref.description: Stable lab-image id this profile pairs with; the comparability axis a metric inherits when it cites this profile.

lab_image_revision.description: Lab-image revision bound to this profile; a recalibration bump resets comparability until a fresh reference capture lands.

permitted_workload_classes.description: Workload classes this profile is approved to back; a metric that uses it outside these classes is non-conforming.

manifest_source_ref.description: Repo-relative canonical register this hardware id projects from (e.g. artifacts/perf/reference_hardware_manifest.yaml).
